To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are relatively few studies that utilize theory to guide understandings of student experiences of interprofessional education in practice based environments.

there are few theoretical frameworks that are used to understand student learning in interprofessional education (IPE) settings and the professional identity and socio-cognitive frameworks are two promising theoretical frameworks that can be used to advance our understanding of student learning in IPE settings.

the theoretical framework used by researchers to understand student learning in interprofessional environments is limited and that there is an opportunity to use theory to advance understandings of student and professional development in interprofessional practice environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical underpinnings of student learning in interprofessional settings.
the development and application of theoretical frameworks for understanding student learning within the context of interprofessional practice-based education.
the theoretical frameworks underpinning student learning in interprofessional education and practice-based environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no comprehensive and detailed conclusive theoretical framework that explains student learning in interprofessional environments.
there is a lack of theoretical-based studies to guide educators and students.
the current body of literature does not provide a strong evidence base to support student learning in interprofessional environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for a more considered use of theory in the study of student learning in interprofessional settings.
we have identified a need for further development of theoretical models of learning in practice-based interprofessional environments.
we have reviewed the current literature on student learning in interprofessional education (IPE) practice-based environments and have identified a lack of theoretical-based research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field of interprofessional education and practice would benefit from a more deliberate approach to the application of theoretical frameworks to student learning in interprofessional settings.

the field of interprofessional education is at an exciting juncture, and that the theoretical frameworks we identify in this paper can be used to inform and guide research in interprofessional practice settings, which in turn can help to advance the field of inter-professional education.
the use of theory can be a powerful tool for advancing understandings and informing future research in the field.
